page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores operating at 2.9 GHz. Hardware caching includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by support for AVX-512 vector instructions and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32.0 GB, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance provides no integrated local storage and operates with a 6 Gbps baseline network throughput without GPU acceleration.

Benchmark assessments establish balanced processing across standardized compute loads. The server logged 1853.98 points in single-core stress-ng and 15550.89 points under multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9594.0 and software compilation score of 15272.0 using Clang. Memory bandwidth registers at 101.79 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 57.38 GB/sec for uncached writes. In lightweight machine learning scenarios, the CPU achieved 266.95 tokens per second during small model text generation, while medium model generation delivered 12.03 tokens per second.

The hardware configuration presents specific architectural tradeoffs. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation prioritizes CPU core density for compute-bound tasks, which limits memory-heavy applications or dense in-memory caches. Because no local disks are provided, storage persistence requires external block storage attachments. These parameters align the instance with continuous integration build runners, batch processing pipelines, static web serving, and containerized microservices where processor core allocation takes precedence over expansive RAM footprints.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.4xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz. It features an x86_64 architecture with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance includes 48 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and no dedicated GPU hardware. Network throughput is provisioned at a 6 Gbps baseline. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent compute capabilities, recording 15550.89 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 9594.0 on Geekbench multi-core workloads, alongside throughput of 266.95 tokens per second in small model LLM text generation. The server fits compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, batch processing, static web serving, and microservices.
